what: the Civilopedia/wikia list of nuclear-blast effects, checked claim by claim against the live game. Two of my own earlier conclusions were WRONG and are corrected here; one wiki claim is contradicted by measurement; one is confirmed in effect but not as a population rule.

verdict: WIKI CORRECT - MY EARLIER FINDING WAS WRONG
reads: pillage correlates perfectly with the blast radius. My earlier 'the wonder is NEVER pillaged, even at ground zero' was a READER ERROR: a wonder is a BUILDING standing on a DISTRICT_WONDER tile, and district:IsPillaged() on that tile reports false whatever happens. The right question is city:GetBuildings():IsPillaged(row.Hash). Ordinary districts answer district:IsPillaged() correctly, which is why the error hid.

claim: Any Districts and buildings in the affected tiles are also pillaged
evidence: every district within radius reads IsPillaged true; every building whose district lies within radius reads buildings:IsPillaged true (MONUMENT, PALACE, GRANARY, WALLS, WATER_MILL, CASTLE, STAR_FORT at dist 0; WORKSHOP at 1; SHRINE, TEMPLE, CATHEDRAL, AMPHITHEATER, MUSEUM_ARTIFACT at 2), while every building at dist 3 reads false (BARRACKS, LIBRARY, ARENA, ARMORY, MILITARY_ACADEMY)
districtsInBlast, districtsTotal and buildingsTotal are identical before and after for all eleven struck cities - nothing is removed from the map, everything in the radius is flagged pillaged

claim: Units occupying the affected tiles are destroyed
evidence: radius-2 device: rings 0,1,2 went 1->0, 7->0, 14->0 and ring 3 was untouched; radius-1 device: rings 0,1 went 1->0, 7->0 and ALL 14 of ring 2 survived at zero damage. 100% inside, 0% outside, no partial damage.

claim: All tiles affected are contaminated with radioactive fallout
evidence: 19 plots (1+6+12) for the radius-2 device, 7 plots (1+6) for radius-1, centred on the AIM PLOT not the city; 20 turns thermonuclear, 10 turns nuclear, uniform. Note Gathering Storm has NO FEATURE_FALLOUT row - the reader is Game.GetFalloutManager():GetFalloutTurnsRemaining(plotIndex).
Farm, Mine, Pasture and Quarry inside the radius all read IsImprovementPillaged true afterwards and false before; improvements outside untouched; routes NOT pillaged

claim: Any City Centers or Encampments caught in the blast will have their HP and Defense Strength reduced to 0

evidence.hp: CONFIRMED - the struck city centre reads garrison 200/200 and outer 300/300, i.e. both pools at maximum damage, zero health
evidence.defenseStrength: CONTRADICTED - the same pillaged city centre reads GetDefenseStrength() = 70, not 0

reads: HP does go to zero; defence strength does not. Either the wiki means the outer/walls contribution, or it is simply wrong about the number this getter returns.

claim: Citizens working the affected tiles are eliminated
reads: both cities had EVERY worked tile inside the blast (pop + the free centre) and both kept their ENTIRE population after a centred thermonuclear that pillaged their city centre. Measured with city:GetCitizens():IsPlotWorked(x,y) - the correct per-city reader; plot:GetWorkerCount() counts any owner's citizens and leaks neighbouring cities in. After the strike the citizens are STILL assigned to the contaminated tiles (tilesWorkedInBlast unchanged at 7 and 6), so the blast neither killed them nor unassigned them.

claim: Any unfinished Districts are destroyed and removed from the map
reads: observed on the CAPTURE path (Shizuoka's incomplete Aqueduct vanished from the district list when the city changed hands), never on a blast - no target in these waves had an incomplete district inside the radius

SENDAI settles the major-versus-minor confound: a MAJOR civilisation's city with exactly TWO complete districts in the blast lost ZERO population. Every city-state that lost nothing also had two. So the driver is the DISTRICT COUNT, not the owner's kind. The rule now rests on: 1 district - OTSU (major) 4->4, AKKAD (minor) 5->5; 2 districts - SENDAI (major) 6->6, NAN_MADOL 7->7, NGAZARGAMU 10->10, MUSCAT 12->11; 3+ districts - OSAKA 8->1, MONTROSE 8->1, NAGOYA 7->1, MEROE 7->1, DUNDEE 12->1, NAPATA 5->3, OKAYAMA 13->6.

<=2 complete districts inside the radius: the city loses 0 or 1 population, whatever its size (a pop-12 city-state lost ONE). >=3: the city is gutted, five of seven straight to population 1. This is deterministic and reproduced across a reload and three timelines. What it is NOT: a function of population, a fraction, a housing clamp, or the number of citizens working the struck tiles.

the wonder error and the citizens error are the same mistake twice: asking a plausible-looking getter on the WRONG OBJECT and believing a clean, consistent answer. district:IsPillaged() on a wonder tile and plot:GetWorkerCount() for a city's citizens both returned tidy numbers for every row, with no error and no nil - the tell was only that they disagreed with an outside source. When a reading contradicts a published description, re-derive the READER before rejecting the description.
